summary: RPCS3 Core 938 = Core 937 plus the fourth part of the heat and energy lot, from the IPA 737 device logs (maintainer, 14 Nov 2026: finish every point left untouched). REWINDBOX_RSX_LONG_IDLE_938: once the RSX FIFO has been empty for 250 ms without a break, the idle park sleeps 1 ms slices instead of 50 us (Black Ops II frozen: 16,600 wakeups a second for nothing; God of War III loading: 9,600); a flush, flip or ZCULL request still wakes it at once, and no game renders with its RSX idle that long between two bursts. REWINDBOX_FREEZE_SPU_MEMORY_938 (measurement only): a busy no-frame freeze that has lasted 20 s writes, once per process, every SPU thread's local store and registers beside the journals (RPCS3-freeze-spu.bin), the code of the jobs the Black Ops II freeze requeues forever, which a game patch must read (the Core 935 flip cause is refuted by the IPA 737 dump). Codegen identities unchanged. Nothing has run on an iPhone. RPCS3 Core 937 = Core 936 plus the third part of the heat and energy lot, from the IPA 737 device logs (maintainer, 14 Nov 2026). REWINDBOX_SPU_IDLE_BACKOFF_937: in the Black Ops II menus at 60 FPS the process still took 48,000 timer wakeups a second, as on IPA 726; 35,000 to 38,000 of them are the 100 us wait of a polling GETLLAR (SPUWAIT551 getllar_sleep, 149 us each on average), a wait the Core 935 rule did not cover. Its bound now follows the same self-validating rule (100, 200, 400 us while it keeps being reached with nothing to find; a notifying write still ends it at once; a change found right after a lengthened bound holds the 100 us bound). Chosen from around process_mfc_cmd(), whose body keeps its Core 610 bytes. Codegen identities unchanged through one exact alias. Nothing has run on an iPhone. RPCS3 Core 936 = Core 935 plus the second part of the heat and energy lot (maintainer, 13 Nov 2026), from five investigations of the IPA 726 device logs. REWINDBOX_PREHASH_IDLE_936: God of War III only (the one title with the texture pre-hash lever): in its 60 FPS scenes the pre-hash worker hashed 0.87 to 0.96 GB per 5 s window for results that were all discarded (52 to 62 ms of CPU, 0 used); it now pauses for 120 frames after three periods with less than one hash in eight used, on frames of at most 16 validations; heavier frames are unchanged. REWINDBOX_WAKE_CENSUS_936 (measurement only): one COREPROF WAKE936 line per window counts the timed waits of guest PPU threads by length and outcome, the slices of the RSX idle park and the polls of the ZCULL on-demand read, the sites the logs could only bound (4,900 to 17,000 wakeups per second estimated for the RSX park). REWINDBOX_PPU_WAIT_SITE_936 (measurement only): the PPU profile adds the flags, last named call and pc of waits outside any named call (God of War III at 60 FPS: the main thread is billed 0.6 to 0.9 performance core while 89 % of its samples are such waits). No codegen input changes. Nothing has run on an iPhone. RPCS3 Core 935 = Core 934 plus the heat and energy lot and the fixes read in device logs (maintainer, 13 Nov 2026: less heat and energy use on iPhone; iPhone logs of IPA 726, ARMSX3 iOS 0.0.2 (3), RPCS3 upstream). REWINDBOX_FLIP_DONE_REPLAY_935: Black Ops II (six serials) froze for good because the game clears the RSX flip done bit after the flip already set it; a flip that found the bit set is given back when the guest clears it within 250 ms (in the frozen state the logs show 5.4 to 5.6 cores and 2.4 to 2.8 W of CPU at 0 FPS). REWINDBOX_SPU_IDLE_BACKOFF_935: the bound of four idle SPU waits (100 us event waits, 160 us polled queue) doubles after 8 empty waits, up to 800 us and 640 us, and checks itself (a find right after a lengthened bound keeps the reference bound for 256, 512, ... waits); its switch is the existing setting Event Waits When Hot (Disabled turns it off; the comparison between report windows drives it); the logs show 44,000 to 80,000 timer wakeups per second in menus. REWINDBOX_NO_GDB_SERVER_935 (ARMSX3 d29f0afe), REWINDBOX_CAMERA_IDLE_935 (ARMSX3 90a50f75) and REWINDBOX_EVENT_WAIT_COUNTER_935 (the WFE latency counter was never read: ';' starts a comment for the Apple assembler). 16-byte atomics: CASPAL compare-exchange and exchange, LSE2 loads and stores on Apple (RPCS3 d4c236fc, b24a3229, 11bcaee2). REWINDBOX_ATOMIC_DMA_LINE_935 (RPCS3 82aaf08c, scoped): a validated whole-line GET; an atomic whole-line PUT with relaxed reservations only. REWINDBOX_CANARY_PATCHES_935: the canary patch file of ARMSX3 iOS 0.0.2 (3) (two Black Ops III BLES02166 patches, on by default). RPCS3 upstream fixes: be7f357b ac5c0e5a 2dca003b 048a59ec c1b25a79 7678217f 23d28a4a b3e3df36 a62b83de 5a5f117a 7ae11e2e 177deabd 0991bacc 5dddfc03 320c29a1 556ed8d1 d540513e 85be81f0 f559420b 8b9a90a3 2cef90e6 5eca8ab3 9b8974d3 965f4f58 de964191 90d8264e a296c261. Codegen identities unchanged (PPU a987639e9f838d1c, SPU 477a3fa442d27917): SPUThread.cpp and SPULLVMRecompiler.cpp change in host code only, each under one exact alias in rpcs3/Emu/CPU/JITCacheCompatibility.cmake. ABI 30 and the 92 exports unchanged. Nothing has run on an iPhone; not compiled for iOS yet. RPCS3 Core 934 = Core 933 plus two fixes of per-game display settings (maintainer, 12 Nov 2026: God of War III no longer stretches). REWINDBOX_SETTINGS_API_RULE_934: the settings API follows the Core 922 boot rule; a legacy full custom_configs file is no longer read by the API either, so the in-game menu shows global < RPCS3 database < the user's sparse overrides, as the boot runs, and a per-game change (Stretch to fill screen included) is saved as a sparse override instead of into the file the boot ignores. REWINDBOX_METAL_STRETCH_934: the native Metal 4 present honours Stretch To Display Area as the Vulkan present does. No codegen input changes. RPCS3 Core 933 = Core 932 plus the local profile of a game (REWINDBOX_LOCAL_PROFILE_933: what this device learned for a serial and game version, bounded, written atomically, ignored for another version) and its first learned decision (REWINDBOX_LEARNED_PREFETCH_933: the Core 616 SPU object prefetch for any title whose play spends at least 500 ms of a window reading cached SPU objects, Automatic only, validated by its hits, withdrawn when unused). No codegen input changes. RPCS3 Core 932 = Core 931 plus the ARMSX3 lot and the first fixes of the maintainer audit (11 Nov 2026): ARMSX3's bundled game fixes on by default, the user's choice saved (REWINDBOX_CANARY_PATCHES_932); database settings a fix makes useless lifted for GT6 and GTA IV, never against the user (REWINDBOX_PATCH_RELIEF_932); Black Ops II levers for its six serials (REWINDBOX_TITLE_VARIANTS_932); energy counters that go back reported invalid, storage traffic, time per thermal state, measured WFE durations (REWINDBOX_ENERGY_VALIDITY_932, REWINDBOX_DISK_IO_932, REWINDBOX_THERMAL_LEDGER_932, REWINDBOX_EVENT_WAIT_LATENCY_932); the background pause asked at the end of a boot (REWINDBOX_BACKGROUND_PAUSE_TRANSITION_932); less speculative texture hashing when warm, a 16 MiB JIT fallback step, Metal concurrent compilation. No codegen input changes. RPCS3 Core 931 = Core 930 plus the thermal chantier (maintainer, 11 Nov 2026): the hot-path counters of the SPU PUTLLC writer lock and of the PPU parks keep one line per thread and the lock's phases are published after its release (REWINDBOX_HOT_COUNTERS_931, REWINDBOX_WRITER_RECORD_AFTER_RELEASE_931); from the serious thermal state three short spins wait with the ARM exclusive monitor, same condition and bound (REWINDBOX_THERMAL_POLICY_931, setting Event Waits When Hot); COREPROF ENERGY931 and THERMAL931 report energy per frame, performance-core share, timer wakeups and the thermal state (REWINDBOX_ENERGY_931); the emulation pauses in the background (REWINDBOX_BACKGROUND_PAUSE_931). No codegen input changes. RPCS3 Core 930 = Core 929 plus the SPU wait sites of the SPU region profile. REWINDBOX_SPU_WAIT_SITE_930: the profile named sys_spu_thread_send_event for 98 % of the waiting samples of Black Ops II (build 725) because spu_thread::current_func is the last named call; each waiting sample is now classified by the thread flags, then by the instruction at the pc the SPU recompiler saves before a blocking call (channel, MFC command, STOP code): wait_sites= on COREPROF SPUPROF923. Diagnostic only; no codegen input changes. RPCS3 Core 929 = Core 928 with the restored memory of a savestate left as saved. REWINDBOX_GOW3_MLAA_SAVESTATE_UNTOUCHED_929 withdraws REWINDBOX_GOW3_MLAA_SAVESTATE_922: Core 922 wrote the God of War III MLAA bypass pair into the restored memory of a savestate made without it, so the game kept running with MLAA set up and its own flag cleared under it. Builds 724 and 725 resumed the savestate build 723 had resumed and the picture broke at the first pause menu, on resumed sessions only (maintainer, 11 Nov 2026); build 723, which left that memory as it was, had no reported defect. The pair is written at a fresh boot only, as upstream applies every executable patch; a savestate made after a fresh boot holds it. No codegen input changes. Core 928 (compiled by run 42960159566), otherwise unchanged: the GPU gate closed when the application is deactivated. REWINDBOX_GPU_DEACTIVATION_GATE_928: Core 927 closed its gate at the background notification; the journal of the only device loss (IPA 650, pid 8767) has "Device lost" 30 ms before the host's own observer of that notification ran, so the command buffer had been refused before the application handled it. Apple's Metal documentation ("Preparing your Metal app to run in the background") gives the procedure the Core now follows: stop sending work when the application is deactivated, make sure what was committed is scheduled when it enters the background, enable the code again once it is reactivated. The gate closes and settles at UIApplicationWillResignActiveNotification; the background notification only finishes what is left (a resumed settle gives the queues nothing new); a renderer created while the application is not active closes the gate at once; the freeze episode sampler counts the closed time as paused; COREPROF GPUGATE928 replaces COREPROF GPUGATE927. While the application is inactive the picture stands still. No codegen input changes. Core 927 (compiled by run 42946503173, pinned as the fallback), otherwise unchanged: asynchronous MoltenVK submits made definitive (maintainer, 11 November 2026: no protection, the lever must work, for every title that needs it). REWINDBOX_MVK_ASYNC_DEFINITIVE_927: the boot record of Cores 587 to 926 is removed and Automatic is every title (synchronous only when the configuration turns asynchronous texture streaming on); in the device journals 16 asynchronous sessions (Assassin's Creed, Black Ops II; 76,148 presents) ran with 0 acquisitions timed out, 0.05 ms of vkQueueSubmit per frame on the RSX thread against 3.5-4.8 ms per Black Ops II frame without them. The order of encoding is kept by waiting: the wait for the last present marker is never abandoned (MoltenVK's event semaphores count when the waiting submit is encoded), every submission of the presenting queue gets a marker and fence waits and occlusion gathers sleep until their submission is encoded instead of spinning. REWINDBOX_GPU_BACKGROUND_GATE_927: the only device loss of the journals (IPA 650) happened as the application entered the background; the Core observes the application, parks submissions, presents, acquisitions and device waits there, lets the queues settle inside the transition and resumes when the application is active. No codegen input changes. Core 926 (compiled by run 42935666936, not pinned), unchanged except the retry of the boot record, which 927 supersedes: REWINDBOX_TEXMEMO_SERVE_BO2_926: Black Ops II ran the texture lookup memo in verify_all on five builds, 4,676,476 reuses compared, 0 differences; its hits are now served with the sampled verification. The Core 925 insertions are moved away from the Core 921/923 lines. No codegen input changes. Core 925 (compiled by run 42930926849, not pinned), unchanged: REWINDBOX_GPU_MEMORY_PACKING_925: IPA 724, Black Ops II, pid 50194 session 8: the bytes the Vulkan allocator handed out plateau at 777-813 MiB while its 64 MiB blocks go from 648 to 1136 MiB and their unused part from 45 to 360 MiB; the kernel graphics ledger follows the blocks (each a placement MTLHeap) and the footprint goes from 3.40 to 4.06 GB in two minutes. iOS only ever used the fastest VMA strategy. With the setting GPU Memory Packing (Automatic = every title) an allocation of 1 MiB or more gets device memory of its own and the others the minimum-memory strategy; COREPROF GPUPACK925. Core 924 (compiled by run 42926781861, not pinned), unchanged: REWINDBOX_GATE_BEFORE_LINE_924: an accurate PUTLLC locked its line (rsrv_unique_lock) and then took vm::writer_lock, whose deferral to a starving PPU and to the window that PPU opens (CELL571, REWINDBOX_PPU_GRACE_664) ran with the line locked, and a PPU conditional store fails on a locked line. IPA 724, Black Ops II, pid 50194: no frame from window 41 on, the main thread on a semaphore, the PPU thread Secondary holding a reservation on 0x2e208d8 whose line word shows another thread's lock on two reads 27 us apart, six SPUs completing 7.5 and 8.5 million PUTLLC per 5 s window on that line with none asleep. The deferral is made before the line is locked and the writer lock does not defer again: same waits, same bound, the same validation of the reservation time and of the line after it. SPUThread.cpp changes in do_putllc() only, with one exact alias: PPU and SPU codegen identities unchanged. Core 923, unchanged: REWINDBOX_SPU_PROFILE_923: God of War III play windows of build 723 run at 9-13 FPS with the GPU busy 14-21 % and five SPU threads at 0.6-0.83 core each, and nothing in the journal says what they run; when the SPU threads use 2.5 cores or more in two consecutive running windows with frames the report asks once per boot (COREPROF AUTOSPU923) for a region profile, and every region profile capture also samples the SPU threads (COREPROF SPUPROF923: state, pc, system call when waiting). REWINDBOX_MEMORY_PARTS_923: COREPROF MEMPARTS923 prints per window what the kernel ledger attributes the footprint to (graphics tag, internal, compressed). Core 922, unchanged: REWINDBOX_GOW3_MLAA_SAVESTATE_922: God of War III resumed from a savestate made without the MLAA bypass ran MLAA (builds 721 and 723: every resumed session reported ppu=savestate_memory savestate_patched=0 and read the 1280x720 colour buffer back 72-107 times per 5 s window at 12-23 FPS; every fresh boot ppu=applied and 0); the guest memory is restored before the executable loader runs, so the same official 01.00 pair, behind the same content guard, is written into the restored memory when it lacks it (GOW3MLAA909 ppu=savestate_applied); the unguarded 01.03 pair is never written into a savestate. REWINDBOX_FREEZE_RESERVATION_922: the Black Ops II freeze of build 723 printed line reservation words below times the SPU and PPU threads held, with bit 64 set; FREEZE_DUMP spu and ppu lines now carry the word of their line read next to the thread time (res=, getllar_res=, with the time-base counter), the PPU last_faddr, last_ftime and last_fail, and line records their read time. REWINDBOX_CONFIG_DATABASE_RULE_922 (maintainer rule): the RPCS3 database is the reference for every game; a legacy full custom_configs file (a snapshot of an earlier RewindBox title profile) is left on disk and no longer applied (CONFIG_DB922), the title runs global < RPCS3 database < the user per-game settings, at the global resolution; the MLAA bypass Automatic mode is on for God of War III. Everything else is Core 921. No reservation, timing, scheduling, resolution, precision, frame limit, SPU count or priority or LLVM option changes. ABI 30, the 92 exports and the PPU/SPU codegen identities unchanged (no codegen input changes). The compile run, the artifact digests and the device status of this Core are recorded in build-utils/rpcs3/core-pin.json and docs/AI_TASK_BOARD.md, not in this summary.
